WHY TRUST IT / READ THE SOURCE

Evidence with context.

Oura’s reported Smart Sensing comparison

Oura describes an August 2024 study with 60 participants comparing Ring 4, Gen3 and reference equipment in a sleep-clinic setting. The reported changes concern specific sensing measures; they are not one accuracy percentage for everything the ring does.

Source: manufacturer-reported research. Individual results can vary.

Read Oura’s study summary
01

Light and pulse

Green and infrared optical sensing follows heart rate. Other optical measurements support overnight blood oxygen insights.

02

Temperature trends

A digital sensor follows average temperature variations. It does not provide the same reading as a clinical thermometer.

03

Movement and fit

An accelerometer captures movement. The correct size and orientation help the ring collect useful signals.

YOUR QUESTIONS, ANSWERED

Before you choose.

Is there one accuracy percentage for the whole ring?

Accuracy depends on the measure, comparison method and study setting. Read claims with their device generation and limitations.

Can Oura Ring 4 diagnose an illness?

Oura supports general wellness insights and is not intended for medical diagnosis. Seek qualified professional advice for health concerns.
